title: Hair Puff
text:
Makes hair stick straight out from its surface normal. Most useful when used alongside an animated vertex group.
Useful for hackles-raising or static electricity type effects. It is also useful to help avoid hairs intersecting each other or the surface mesh if the surface bends at extreme angles, while being much lighter than hair physics. An advanced usecase could be to combine this with tension mapping to help avoid fur intersecting on the inside of elbows, etc..
Also, when used after Hair Curl, it uncurls the hairs. This can be used to fake springiness.

title: (WIP) One Hand
text:
Pie menus and special navigation, selection, and transformation controls that let you use Blender with ONLY one hand and a mouse or tablet! You’ll probably want an on-screen keyboard to help you type vertex group names, enter numbers, etc., but besides that, trust me, it’s epic.
Inspired by Flow Navigation. I LOVE that addon (I recommend at least trying out the free Lite version, it will change your life). However, I had to edit it a bit to get it exactly how I wanted, plus it lagged my viewport and I found its UI annoying. I wanted my own simpler alterative.

title: (WIP) pCloudstream
text:
Use an XBox Kinect to stream a 3D pointcloud directly into Blender, live!
The USB bandwidth of a single computer is limited, so I’m making it so that you can send data from Kinects connected to other computers, over a network.
Currently I can stream at about 5FPS. However, there are many optimizations still up for grabs:

Don’t send dead points where xyz==0,0,0. These happen when a surface is too close/far to the Kinect.
Options to quantize XYZ and RGB data
Randomly cull some proportion of the points before sending.
Send info from the receiver (running Blender) to the senders (connected to Kinects) to:

Cull outside a camera’s frustom
Cull outside a certain box area (e.g. to only send a pointcloud of your body and not the walls of the room)
Cull points of a certain color (e.g. to precisely cull a room’s floor even if it is touching your feet)

Fix the memory leak in my current implementation…

Overall these optimizations should easily quadruple the FPS at least, so I’m optimistic about being able to livestream pointclouds at high framerates and low performance cost.
Here’s a picture of my room streamed into Blender. (The ugly striping will go away once I implement vsync.)

title: (WIP) Leap 4 Blender
text:
Remember those LeapMotion hand trackers? Well now you can use them to livestream hand mocap into Blender! Even nowadays with AI, Leap trackers are the best hand mocap you can get for the $10-$100 pricerange. Arguably it’s even better than mocap gloves which are multiple times that price. Unfortunately the company went out of business, but you can still get a device pretty easily. All you need is some patience on EBay.
The advantage of accellerometer-based devices like gloves over optical devices like Leap, is you don’t have to worry about your palm blocking the device from seeing your fingers. However, if you can work around this limitation, there is no better accuracy than optical mocap. You get sub-milimeter precision and no jittering.
Demo below (the GIF is at 10FPS which doesn’t do it justice, in reality it’s at a smooth 60FPS).

title: (WIP) Sticky GP
text:
Lets you draw Grease Pencil on a deformed mesh, and have it stick as the mesh deforms further.
How it works: similar to the hair system, it simply records the UV coordinate of the mesh where a GP point is drawn. Then there is an accompanying geonodes group that sets the position of each GP point to the 3D position corresponding to that UV coordinate. It’s so simple, and I’ve seen so many people ask for this functionality, and yet no one has done it yet as far as I can tell?! There are a few solutions out there but they all require you to draw on the resting position of the mesh. There was a PR for a GP surface deform modifier a couple years ago, but it fizzled out.
Especially in combination with the Build modifier allows you to animate vertex groups in a very art-directible way!

title: Hair Mask
text:
This improves performance by deleting hairs based on distance to some “mask” empties. This allows you to groom small regions of fur with high density or heavy modifiers in real time, so you can immediately see how your grooming will affect the final look.

Delete hairs by distance
Deletes hairs if their root is outside the mask.


Delete hairs by distance to surface mesh
Deletes hairs if their root is stuck to a face of the surface mesh outside the mask. the This is a slightly less accurate, but probably faster approach since there are usually fewer vertices in the hairs’ surface mesh than in the hairs themselves.

title: Groomviz
text:
This nodegroup colors hairs based on useful attributes, intended for use while working on a groom.
To use, simply plug into the Material Output surface, and be in viewport Material Preview or Rendered mode. TODO IMAGE

Hairtips
Gives a good sense of the hair density, volume, and direction all at the same time while not being overwhelming.
To purely visualize the hair’s volume, you can set the root color to be transparent so only hairtips are visible.


Tangent
Colors hairs depending on the direction they are pointing. Great way to catch abrupt changes in hair direction which usually look bad.


Hairlength (animated)
Great way to catch any abrupt changes in hair length which usually look bad.
TODO GIF


Rainbow
Another way to visualize hair length. Not that useful, but looks rad.


Attribute
Color hair based on a named attribute, such as from geonodes.


Passthrough
Simply outputs the material given in the Passthrough input. This is so you can easily switch to your own hair material using the menu dropdown list, without having to replug any node connector noodles.
